title: DOWN from a bodyless probe result is preserved, not overwritten with UNKNOWN

steps.action: Provision an availability/service-check monitor and force the probe to return an event whose top-level status is DOWN with a null result body (probe timed out or errored before producing a body) on a PING monitor
steps.expected: The collector emits status=DOWN with result=null

steps.action: Read the object status recorded in ObjectStatusCacheStore for that monitor
steps.expected: Status is DOWN. The guard at CollectorResponseProcessor.java:191 / ResponseProcessor.java:634 must read !isUP && !isDOWN; with the shipped || it is a tautology and always overwrites to UNKNOWN. Expect a fail until fixed

steps.action: Open the monitor availability history for that interval
steps.expected: A DOWN interval is recorded — not an UNKNOWN gap

title: UP from a bodyless probe result is preserved, not overwritten with UNKNOWN

steps.action: Force a successful probe whose event carries status=UP with a null result body
steps.expected: Event reaches the PING..CERTIFICATE case branch

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: Status is UP. The tautological guard clobbers UP to UNKNOWN just as it does DOWN — both rows of the truth table evaluate true

title: An explicit status in the result body still wins over the event status

steps.action: Force a probe whose result body contains status=DOWN while the event top-level status is UP
steps.expected: The first branch fires because result != null && result.containsKey(STATUS)

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: Status is DOWN — taken from the result body, and the UNKNOWN normalisation branch is never reached

title: A genuinely indeterminate status is still normalised to UNKNOWN

steps.action: Force a probe whose event status is neither UP nor DOWN (e.g. an empty or garbage status) with a null result body
steps.expected: The normalisation branch is reached

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: Status is UNKNOWN. Fixing || to && must NOT remove this behaviour — the branch has to still fire for a value that is neither UP nor DOWN

title: DOWN-triggered alert policy fires for a bodyless DOWN probe

steps.action: Create an availability alert policy that triggers on DOWN for a PING monitor, then provision an availability/service-check monitor and force the probe to return an event whose top-level status is down with a null result body (probe timed out or errored before producing a body)
steps.expected: Policy is active and the probe reports DOWN

steps.action: Check Active Alerts
steps.expected: A DOWN alert is raised for the monitor. This is the customer-visible symptom of the bug — a real outage currently produces no alert

title: Availability report shows downtime, not an UNKNOWN gap

steps.action: Produce a bodyless DOWN interval on a monitor, then run the availability report for that window
steps.expected: Report generates

steps.action: Inspect the interval
steps.expected: It is counted as downtime. Currently it lands as UNKNOWN, which understates the outage

title: SLO/availability percentage accounts for the DOWN interval

steps.action: Note the availability percentage for a monitor, force a 10-minute bodyless DOWN interval, then re-read it
steps.expected: Percentage is recalculated

steps.action: Compare
steps.expected: Availability drops by the outage duration. An UNKNOWN gap must not silently preserve a 100% figure

steps.action: Provision a PING service-check monitor and force a bodyless DOWN probe result
steps.expected: Probe reports DOWN with result=null

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: Status is DOWN. All of PING, PORT, NTP, RADIUS, FTP, URL, DOMAIN, EMAIL, CERTIFICATE share the one case branch, so every plugin in the family regresses together and must be verified together

title: EdgeCollector topology preserves a reported DOWN

steps.action: Deploy with an EdgeCollector and route an availability monitor through it, then force a bodyless DOWN
steps.expected: Event flows through CollectorResponseProcessor

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: Status is DOWN. This is the collector-side copy of the defect at CollectorResponseProcessor.java:191

title: Standalone/Primary topology preserves a reported DOWN

steps.action: On a Standalone or Primary deployment, force a bodyless DOWN on an availability monitor
steps.expected: Event flows through ResponseProcessor

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: Status is DOWN. This is the app-side copy at ResponseProcessor.java:634 — no deployment topology is unaffected, so both must be fixed and both tested

title: AVAILABILITY plugin ABORT carries forward the previous status

steps.action: Drive an AVAILABILITY-plugin monitor to a known UP state, then force an event with status=ABORT (poller over-utilisation)
steps.expected: The ABORT branch fires

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: The previously cached status (UP) is carried forward from ObjectStatusCacheStore, not reset. Only an object with no cached entry becomes UNKNOWN

title: AVAILABILITY plugin ABORT on a never-polled object yields UNKNOWN

steps.action: Force an ABORT event for an AVAILABILITY monitor that has no entry in ObjectStatusCacheStore yet
steps.expected: The ABORT branch fires and existItem() is false

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: Status is UNKNOWN — the documented fallback when nothing was cached

title: AVAILABILITY plugin non-ABORT failure records DOWN

steps.action: Force a non-ABORT failure event for an AVAILABILITY-plugin monitor
steps.expected: The else branch fires

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: Status is DOWN — written unconditionally by that branch, independent of the PING..CERTIFICATE guard

title: Status transition UP to DOWN to UP is recorded with correct timestamps

steps.action: Drive a monitor UP, then bodyless DOWN, then UP again across three polls
steps.expected: Three events processed

steps.action: Inspect the availability history
steps.expected: Exactly one DOWN interval bounded by the two poll timestamps; ObjectStatusCacheStore.updateItem is called with each event timestamp, so no interval is lost or merged

title: Fix does not introduce flapping on repeated identical DOWN polls

steps.action: Force five consecutive bodyless DOWN probes on one monitor
steps.expected: All five processed

steps.action: Check Active Alerts and availability history
steps.expected: One continuous DOWN interval and one alert — not five alerts and not five intervals

title: Concurrent probe results for many monitors do not cross-contaminate status

steps.action: Force bodyless results simultaneously across 50 monitors — half DOWN, half UP
steps.expected: All processed

steps.action: Read every recorded status
steps.expected: Each monitor holds its own reported status; no monitor picks up another's value and none is UNKNOWN

title: default plugin branch still handles a failed ping check by error code

steps.action: Force an event for a non-availability plugin carrying pingCheckStatus=NO and a known error code
steps.expected: The default branch fires

steps.action: Inspect the resulting status and error handling
steps.expected: The error-code switch drives the outcome; the UP/DOWN normalisation guard is not involved and its fix must not change this path

title: Monitor status tile and inventory reflect DOWN immediately

steps.action: Force a bodyless DOWN on a monitored device and watch the Monitors inventory and dashboard severity tiles
steps.expected: Status propagates

steps.action: Compare tile counts before and after
steps.expected: The device moves into the DOWN count, not into UNKNOWN

title: Existing UNKNOWN behaviour for an unreachable collector is unchanged

steps.action: Stop the collector polling a monitor so no probe result arrives at all
steps.expected: No event is produced

steps.action: Read the recorded object status
steps.expected: The pre-existing no-data handling applies unchanged; the || to && fix must not alter the genuinely-unknown case

title: Unit test coverage exists for all three truth-table rows

steps.action: Review the automated tests covering the normalisation branch after the fix
steps.expected: Tests exist

steps.action: Confirm the cases asserted
steps.expected: UP stays UP, DOWN stays DOWN, and a neither-UP-nor-DOWN value becomes UNKNOWN — the three rows the ticket tabulates. A fix without all three is under-tested

title: Both call sites are fixed, not just one

steps.action: Review ResponseProcessor.java around line 634 and CollectorResponseProcessor.java around line 191
steps.expected: Both sites visible

steps.action: Compare the guards
steps.expected: Both read && — the code is byte-identical in the two files, so fixing one and shipping leaves half the deployments broken
